UpdateOrderStateUseCase.ts: execute returns the same mapping, copied inline
ListOrdersByStateUseCase.ts: execute maps orders with the same shape, copied inline

DTOs.ts: UpdateOrderStateRequest and CancelOrderRequest are declared but no use case uses them
CancelOrderUseCase.ts: if (currentState === 'shipped' || currentState === 'delivered') throw ... and then order.transitionTo('cancelled')
PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: if (product.getStock() < item.quantity) throw ... and then product.reserve(item.quantity)

parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module has one clear concern: order and product use cases with their DTOs. It fails the rubric because some rules are written in more than one place.

1. The mapping from an Order to its response shape is written out three times. PlaceOrderUseCase puts it in a private toResponse. UpdateOrderStateUseCase and ListOrdersByStateUseCase each copy the same id/customerId/state/items/createdAt mapping inline. There is no shared mapper.

2. DTOs.ts repeats one order shape three times. CreateOrderResponse and UpdateOrderStateResponse are identical, and ListOrdersResponse writes the same shape inline. It also declares UpdateOrderStateRequest and CancelOrderRequest, which no use case uses. UpdateOrderStateUseCase.execute takes a bare (orderId, newState) instead of UpdateOrderStateRequest.

3. CancelOrderUseCase decides for itself which states can be cancelled (shipped/delivered) and then calls order.transitionTo('cancelled'). That copies the state-transition rule, which belongs to Order.transitionTo, the method UpdateOrderStateUseCase relies on alone.

4. PlaceOrderUseCase checks product.getStock() < item.quantity itself before calling product.reserve(). Reserving stock is the Product's job, and this check appears to repeat it.

5. GetProductStockUseCase writes the Product-to-ProductStockResponse mapping twice, in execute and in executeAll.

6. ListOrdersByStateUseCase injects a productRepository it never uses.
